title.en: Operations without a thermal envelope: mixing, cutting, peeling

goal.en: Not every operation has a temperature band. Mixing has no envelope at all and is verified by time; cutting and peeling have an envelope without temperatures, with hazards and a ladder but nothing for a thermometer to check.

note.en: A trace for mixing: nothing thermal to check, so envelopeOk is true with the reason no_thermal_envelope.
The same for cutting, which has an envelope but no temperature band.
Mixing has no ladder in the vocabulary; the default is time.
Peeling has a ladder (vision, then a person) and no time rung: alone, null.
In the vocabulary: mix has no envelope; peel has one that says unattended is false and names the cut hazard.
Time for mixing, nothing for peeling alone.

cli: printf '[{"t": 0, "tempC": 20}]' > trace.json && cookwala envelope cw.op.mix trace.json
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:7878/v1/tools/ladder -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"op": "cw.op.mix", "sensors": [], "allowModel": false, "humanPresent": false}'
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:7878/v1/tools/ladder -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"op": "cw.op.peel", "sensors": [], "allowModel": true, "humanPresent": false}'

outcome.en: You know the three shapes an operation can take: a thermal envelope, an envelope with hazards and a ladder but no band, or no envelope at all, and how each behaves in the two checks.
